observed_original_abi.calling_convention: __thiscall (ECX carries the receiver and is dereferenced before any definite write; bare RET with no immediate; no stack word read as an argument)
observed_original_abi.receiver: ECX, read at 0x00b8dab0 as the base of the single memory operand `dword ptr [ECX + 0x194]`; never saved to another register and never written
observed_original_abi.return_semantics: the 32-bit word STORED at receiver+0x194, copied bit for bit into EAX
observed_original_abi.return_type_rationale: MODELLED AS A SCALAR, AGAINST THE DERIVED RECORD'S CLASS. The body is two instructions and the opcode is 0x8b (MOV r32, r/m32), so it is a LOAD of a stored word and not a LEA of an address. Four sampled callers use the result in SIGNED ordered comparisons - 0x00ae5880 `cmp eax,0x5 / jz`, 0x00bd8a4a `cmp eax,0x5 / jnz`, 0x00bade0f `cmp eax,0x2 / jl`, 0x00c8b60e `cmp eax,[esp+0x10] / jle` - and 0x00c8b616 folds it into a running maximum; none dereferences it. The derived ABI record classifies the EAX value `register_class: pointer_like` on a single heuristic (the last value written to EAX) with `confidence: INFERRED` and `corroboration: not_available`; that heuristic cannot distinguish a loaded word from a computed address, so the callers win and the disagreement is recorded rather than adopted.
observed_original_abi.locals: none; the body allocates no frame, saves no register and builds no record
observed_original_abi.outgoing_calls: none; the body holds no CALL, no JMP and no indirect transfer

observed_mechanics: 0x00b8dab0 8b 81 94 01 00 00 - MOV EAX,dword ptr [ECX + 0x194]: ModRM 0x81 is mod=10 (a disp32 follows), reg=000 (EAX), rm=001 (ECX); the disp32 is 0x00000194.
0x00b8dab6 c3 - RET: single exit; the callee pops nothing, so stack cleanup is 0 bytes and owned by the caller.
The body is 7 bytes (0x00b8dab0..0x00b8dab6) and contains no branch, no call, no flag test, no register save and no loop: the read at +0x194 is unconditional, so every entry reads the same word.
The read happens on every entry: no lazy path, no cache, no publication check, no default and no refresh. A published zero comes back as a published zero.
Nothing is written. The word at +0x194 is not modified by this function and neither is any neighbouring word.

The load/LEA distinction is decidable from the opcode and is not hypothetical in this family: 0x00b8dad0 is `lea eax,[ecx+0x198]` and 0x00b8da60 is `lea eax,[ecx+0x188]`, both two-entry neighbours of this one.
Raw bytes at 0x00b8dab0..0x00b8dab8, read live from the program database: 8b 81 94 01 00 00 c3 cc. The 0xcc at 0x00b8dab7 is INT3 padding between this entry and the next and is NOT part of the body.

field_offsets.note: No field of any type is NAMED. The receiver record is bounds_only ('where the body was SEEN reaching', not a layout), so the one displacement below is a value and not a member identity. The displacement is spelled literally in the source.

receiver.listing_evidence: 0x00b8dab0 is `8b 81 94 01 00 00`; the disp32 is 0x00000194 and the ModRM byte selects ECX as the base
receiver.modelling_use: the receiver fixture is sized to 0x198 so the word at +0x194 is addressable; that extent is a MODELLING BOUND, not a recovered object size, even though sibling accessors in the same block also touch +0x198 and +0x19c

field_offsets.sibling_note: Read from a read-only objdump disassembly of the pinned image over 0x00b8d900..0x00b8dd00. These are what the NEIGHBOURING functions in the same accessor block address; this function reaches exactly one of them (+0x194), and it is the only access to [ECX+0x194] anywhere in that 0x400-byte window. No layout, field name or object size follows from the adjacency.

globals_note: None. The body names no absolute data address; the only memory operand is receiver-relative through ECX. knowledgegraph/triage/datarefs-2540f2ca.tsv records no data reference out of 0x00b8dab0, which is a recorded absence and not a missing read.
vtables_note: None recorded. knowledgegraph/triage/datarefs-2540f2ca.tsv contains ZERO rows for 0x00b8dab0, so on this pinned snapshot it is not the target of any recorded data reference - consistent with the 78/78 direct-call edges in xrefs-2540f2ca.tsv and with the body's zero indirect dispatch. A function reached only through a vtable would appear as the target of a data reference from its table; this is a recorded absence, not an exhaustive proof that no table exists.

types.name: OpaqueReceiver
types.note: sized to the single reached displacement 0x194 plus its four bytes; no member is declared and no class is asserted. The word at 0x194 is UNNAMED.

type_scope: The reconstructed symbol takes an opaque receiver pointer and returns a 32-bit scalar. That the word is consumed as an ORDERED SCALAR is OBSERVED (four callers compare it signed). Which game concept the scalar names is UNKNOWN and is not claimed.

analogues.relation: immediate next entry, `lea eax,[ecx+0x198]` - the LEA contrast case, same receiver family, one displacement word further on
`lea eax,[ecx+0x188]` - the other LEA in the block, showing both forms occur around this receiver
`mov eax,[ecx+0x184] ; sub eax,0x1000000 ; ret` - a LOAD of a neighbouring word plus arithmetic, i.e. the same MOV form with a transform this target does not have

`mov eax,[esp+4] ; mov [ecx+0x184],eax ; ret 0x4` - the SETTER for the neighbour +0x184, which establishes the family's thiscall shape with one stack argument and callee cleanup; this target is the opposite end of that shape
`mov eax,[ecx+0x2c] ; shr eax,2 ; and al,1 ; ret` - a load of a different word of the same receiver, transformed

the immediate call-site receiver source in the sampled callers: it returns `dword [esi+0x13c]` (or 0) and the result is moved into ECX before the call, so the receiver arrives from a field of another object

semantic_findings: The entry is a receiver-field scalar getter: one 32-bit load at displacement 0x194, one return, no validation, no transformation, no write.
78 direct callsites across 30 distinct caller functions in the committed xrefs export, all static. Fan-in says nothing about the field's meaning and is not used as evidence for one.

The returned word is used by four sampled callers in SIGNED ordered comparisons against small constants (0x5 with JZ/JNZ, 0x2 with JL) and as a running maximum reduced with JLE, so the value behaves like an ordinal or threshold rather than an address.

0x00b8dab0 is the only access to [ECX+0x194] in the 0x400-byte accessor window 0x00b8d900..0x00b8dd00, so the getter has no setter in that window; absence of a direct writer is never an immutability claim and this package makes no claim about writers beyond it.

The same accessor block contains both MOV loads and LEA address computations against this receiver, so the load form at this entry is a real distinction in this family rather than a stylistic assumption.
The derived ABI record's `pointer_like` return class is contradicted by the callers' scalar use; the disagreement is recorded and the model follows the callers.
not_claimed: Any name for the word at receiver+0x194, and any name for the receiver's class. UNKNOWN; the receiver record is bounds_only and the type below is opaque.
What the scalar MEANS. `cmp eax,0x5` and `cmp eax,0x2` say it behaves like an ordinal or threshold, but nothing in the evidence pack names a game concept for it.
Any writer of the word at +0x194 beyond the 0x400-byte window scanned, and any immutability or publication claim for it.
The receiver's size or layout. 0x198 is a modelling bound through the one word the body reads, not a recovered allocation size, even though sibling accessors reach +0x19c.

Signedness at the source level. The body copies bits; the signed reading comes from the CALLERS' JL/JLE comparisons, which is why the return type is unsigned and the test models the signed comparisons explicitly.
Any nullability, thread-safety or AddRef/Release ownership for the receiver.
That this entry is or is not reachable through a vtable beyond the recorded zero data references in the pinned sidecar.
Any runtime, Wine, trace, differential or OBSERVED-behaviour claim. No runtime evidence exists for this VA.
confidence: high for the mechanism (two instructions, one displacement, one bare RET), none for the field identity or the scalar's meaning
unresolved_questions: What does the word at receiver+0x194 mean? Four callers show ordinal/threshold behaviour (compared against 2 and 5, reduced with JLE) but no SDK import, committed note or sampled caller names the concept.
Which class is the receiver? Every sampled caller reaches it through FUN_010212a0, i.e. `dword [esi+0x13c]` of another object, and nothing names the resulting class.
Who writes the word at +0x194, and when? No access to [ECX+0x194] exists in the 0x400-byte window 0x00b8d900..0x00b8dd00, but indirect or bulk publication outside that window is unexcluded.

Are the sibling words of this receiver related - +0x184 (which HAS a setter at 0x00b8da80 and a transform getter at 0x00b8da70), +0x188 (LEA only), +0x190 (written at 0x00b8da48), +0x198 (LEA getter, setter at 0x00b8dae6) and +0x19c (written at 0x00b8daef) - a single structure whose fields mean different things, or independent slots? Adjacency in the accessor block is not a layout.
Does the receiver need an AddRef, and by whom? The body has no room for a reference call, so ownership is undetermined.

focused_test.assertion_style: abort on the first failure; each group names the hypothesis it refutes
coverage: the return is the word STORED at +0x194: not the address of it (the LEA form), not the receiver, not the displacement, not a mask/shift/increment of the value

0x194 is a byte displacement and not an index: the planted word at +0x190 and the words at +0x000/+0x004 are all different and none is returned, and the disp32-as-element-count reading lands at byte 0x650, past the modelled extent
the body reads: the whole 0x198-byte receiver is byte-identical before and after the call

the value crosses verbatim: 0, 1, 2, 5, 6, INT_MAX, INT_MIN, 0xfffffffe, 0xffffffff and a 4x4 sweep of the byte pattern all come back unchanged, so no default, mask, sign-extension or saturation survives

the sampled callers' ordered comparisons reproduce: the recorded encodings of `cmp eax,0x2 / jl` and `cmp eax,[esp+0x10] / jle` are pinned, and the signed running-maximum idiom of 0x00c8b609/0x00c8b616 is modelled over both positive and top-bit-set values

the ABI is measured, not asserted: ESP is sampled before the call and after the return and must agree (the callee pops nothing), the receiver arrives in ECX with nothing pushed, and a second receiver at a different address yields a different answer

the encoding is the observed seven bytes, ModRM 0x81 decodes as mod=10/reg=EAX/rm=ECX, the disp32 equals the header's displacement, the opcode is 0x8b and not 0x8d (LEA), the tail is a bare 0xc3 and not 0xc2, and the 0xcc pad is named
the entry's literal displacement and the header's kFieldDisplacement name one and the same address
